name: Anomaly of the Tricuspid Subvalvular Apparatus

criteria.description: Echocardiographic visualization of abnormal or malformed tricuspid subvalvular apparatus including chordae tendineae and papillary muscles
Presence of tricuspid valve regurgitation or stenosis secondary to subvalvular apparatus anomaly
Clinical evidence of right-sided heart failure such as hepatomegaly or peripheral edema in absence of other causes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Echocardiographic identification of abnormal tricuspid subvalvular apparatus plus evidence of tricuspid valve dysfunction
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis primarily relies on imaging; genetic testing may be supportive if familial cases identified

pathognomonic.symptomName: Echocardiographic evidence of malformed tricuspid chordae tendineae
searchTerms: abnormal tricuspid valve chords on ultrasound

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe tricuspid regurgitation due to subvalvular apparatus anomaly

laboratory: Elevated liver enzymes secondary to hepatic congestion
imaging: Echocardiography showing malformed tricuspid subvalvular apparatus
Cardiac MRI confirming structural abnormalities and right atrial enlargement
genetic: Potential familial mutations affecting cardiac valve development genes (e.g., NKX2-5, NOTCH1) in some cases
other: Hemodynamic studies demonstrating tricuspid valve dysfunction

distinguishingFeatures: Apical displacement of tricuspid valve leaflets
More extensive leaflet malformation than isolated subvalvular apparatus anomaly
Presence of vegetations on valve leaflets

redFlags: Progressive right heart failure symptoms despite medical management
Severe tricuspid regurgitation with hemodynamic compromise
references: Anderson RH, et al. The anatomy of the tricuspid valve and its subvalvular apparatus. Heart. 2014.
